memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood. - Gen 22:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The moment arrives. Abraham builds the altar, arranges the wood, and - with what agony we can only imagine - binds his son and lays him on it. Every step is described slowly, deliberately, and each one must have cost Abraham more than we can know. He obeyed all the way to the very edge of the unthinkable.

We should not overlook Isaac in this scene. He was old enough to carry the wood up a mountain, and surely strong enough to resist an elderly father. Yet he allowed himself to be bound and laid on the altar. There is a quiet submission here that, again, points forward to another Son who willingly submitted, who "did not open his mouth" and was "led like a lamb to the slaughter" (Isa 53:7).

This is the climax of Abraham's test - the point where trust is proven not in word but in action. Anyone can say they trust God; Abraham demonstrated it on the mountain, with the knife in his hand and his son on the altar. His faith was not mere feeling; it moved his hands to obey.

There is a searching question here for us. We speak of surrendering everything to God - but do we actually lay it on the altar? True faith is not only believing the right things but trusting God enough to obey Him with our most precious things. What has God asked you to place on the altar of trust? Faith is proven when belief becomes obedience.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there something you say you've surrendered but haven't truly laid on the altar?
- How is your faith proven in action, not just words?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, it is easy to say I trust You; help me prove it in action. Give me faith that moves my hands to obey, willing to lay even my most precious things on the altar of trust in You.
Amen.
